content.thinking: I should adjust the root_cause wording slightly and drop the "a week's" phrasing in CF-1.

action_items.item: Run the one-off repair script from Code-Fix's draft pull request against the account store before the month rolls over: first in its default report-only mode, then with --write once the report has been checked.
Find out which monthly statements and spend summaries were produced from the short month totals since the onset, and whether any reached shoppers.

Make sure any rollback or fix that is deployed also covers the derive_the_month path. At the revision being rolled back to, record_purchase_deriving_the_month also leaves the month total unchanged, so rolling back alone stops new damage only for purchases recorded with derive_the_month off.
Run reconcile_monthly_totals on a schedule much shorter than {A5} days, or after writes, so drift between stored totals and purchases is found soon after it starts.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires.
Add a test that recording a purchase through record_a_purchase with derive_the_month off leaves an account in which reconcile_monthly_totals finds nothing wrong.
Require review to list the readers of a stored field (such as total_this_month_cents) before a change stops writing it, and require deployed revisions to come from reviewed history on main.

causal_chain.step: The stored monthly spend totals stopped matching the purchases behind them: {A1} of the {A2} shopper totals checked did not reconcile, the widest was short by {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at {A4}. The statement and spend-summary code reads that stored total. No error rate was measured, and the shop's takings did not fall by more than they normally vary.

Every purchase recorded since then was written without updating the stored month total. At the running revision, both write paths (record_purchase, and record_purchase_deriving_the_month, which record_a_purchase picks between) add the price only to total_cents. The reconciliation check compares the stored month total with the sum of this month's purchase prices, so each purchase this month opens a gap the size of its price.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of 4c810f2 at {P1.1}: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after the later deploy of 26f1d7e.
A flag change just before the onset: the flag provider's history shows {T16.2} changes by anyone but Argus in the {T16.3} hour before {T16.4}.

causal_chain.step: Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at {P2.1}, took the conditional month-total addition out of record_purchase, the path used when derive_the_month is off. The path used when it is on already left the month total unchanged, so after this change no path updated it. As of {T13.1}, all {T13.2} replicas ran this revision. The oldest affected purchase, at {A4}, comes after this deploy.

The change broke the service because it stopped writing a field that other code still reads. The new docstring says the month figure will be added up from purchase history whenever it is wanted. But the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation code still read total_this_month_cents directly, and the module itself says the running totals exist so that pages do not have to sum a shopper's whole history. Nothing changed those readers.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A software update changed how purchases are recorded so that the shop stopped updating each shopper's running total for the month, but other parts of the shop still read that total as if it were current.

contributing_factors.factor: The only thing seen watching for stored totals drifting from purchases was the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. The request-level series stayed flat because the service kept serving normally.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check run more often would have found the gap soon after the deploy, before most of the short purchases were written.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or review was seen that would catch a write path no longer updating a field that statement, summary and reconciliation code still read. Code-Fix reports that the deployed revision is not in main's history.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The change would have been stopped before it was deployed, even though it still dropped the month-total update.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert was not linked to any on-call incident, so nobody was paged when it fired.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been asked straight away to roll back and repair the totals, rather than the recommendation waiting to be noticed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

got_lucky: The alert fired before the month rolled over. According to Code-Fix's reading, the repair depends on the in_current_month marks on stored purchases still describing the damaged month, and a later onset in the month could have pushed discovery past that point.
went_well: The Investigator read the diff of the suspect deployment {T12.1 - alert_raised} after the alert. That diff showed directly that the month-total update had been removed.
Code-Fix proposed a fix, new tests and a one-off repair script as a draft pull request {T21.1 - alert_raised} after the alert.
went_wrong: Neither candidate noticed that at the running revision record_purchase_deriving_the_month also leaves the month total unchanged. The recommended rollback therefore would not stop new damage for purchases recorded with derive_the_month on.

input.root_cause: The change took the month-total addition out of record_purchase, so that no write path still moves total_this_month_cents: record_purchase_deriving_the_month already left it unchanged. The change rests on the idea that the month figure can be worked out from purchase history whenever it is needed, but the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation code all still read the stored field. Each purchase this month therefore leaves that field short by the purchase's price.
input.still_at_risk: The running revision still records every purchase without updating the stored month total, so each new purchase this month adds to the shortfall that statements and spend summaries read, and the totals already written stay wrong until a person rewrites them; Code-Fix's reading says that rewrite has to happen before the month rolls over.
input.symptom: Shoppers' stored spend totals for the month fell behind the purchases they made
